The patient presents with atrial fibrillation, which is a cardiac arrhythmia characterized by irregular and rapid atrial activation and disorganized atrial contractions. Adenosine is a short-acting antiarrhythmic medication that can be used to convert atrial fibrillation to sinus rhythm. Adenosine works by acting on the A1 adenosine receptors in the heart, which can slow down the heart rate and increase the conductivity of the atrioventricular (AV) node. Therefore, it is the best option to decrease the patient's pulse rate in this scenario. The other options, digoxin, enalapril, and lidocaine, are not indicated for this specific situation. Digoxin is a cardiac glycoside that can be used to slow down the heart rate, but it is not the most effective or safe option in this case, as the patient is already in atrial fibrillation and has a normal blood pressure. Enalapril is an angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor used for the treatment of heart failure and hypertension, and it is not indicated for the rapid control of heart rate in this patient.
